activity_context.topic_title: Marginal Distributions for Discrete Random Variables

examples.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ |

Given the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ above for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y,$ find the marginal mass function for $X.$
examples.worked_solution:
If the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have joint distribution with joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & ={f}_{X}(x)={\sum }_{y}f(x,y) \\ P(Y=y) & ={f}_{Y}(y)={\sum }_{x}f(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

where $f_X(x)$ and $f_Y(y)$ are the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

In this case, the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Let's add these row and column totals to our table:

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $f_X$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0.3}$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0.7}$ |
| $f_Y$ | $0.4$ | $0.6$ | $1$ |

Finally, the marginal mass function for $X$ is given by the following table:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $f_X(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.7$ |

Given the joint probability distribution $f(x,y)$ below for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y,$ find $P(Y=2).$

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
If the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have joint distribution with joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & ={f}_{X}(x)={\sum }_{y}f(x,y) \\ P(Y=y) & ={f}_{Y}(y)={\sum }_{x}f(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

In this case, the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Let's add these row and column totals to our table:

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.5$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.3$ | $0.7$ | $1$ |

Finally, using the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=2) & ={f}_{Y}(2) \\  & =f(1,2)+f(1,2) \\  & =0.4+0.3 \\  & =0.7.\end{aligned}
$$
